findings.description: Intensive glycaemic control arm targets near-normal glucose in a high-risk population (older adults with long-standing Type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease) without sufficiently conservative hypoglycaemia risk stratification or exclusion.
findings.recommendation: Apply stricter exclusion for severe hypoglycaemia history, advanced frailty, and comorbidities; implement adaptive stopping rules tied to serious hypoglycaemic events.
findings.actual_outcome: ACCORD was terminated early due to excess mortality in the intensive arm, with post hoc analyses implicating hypoglycaemia and rapid glucose lowering as potential contributors.

findings.description: Inclusion criteria allow adults ≥40 years with CVD or ≥55 years with additional risk factors, but the risk profile is skewed toward older, highly comorbid patients, increasing vulnerability to intensive treatment harms.
findings.recommendation: Clarify age stratification and incorporate upper age limits or frailty assessments to reduce exposure of very high-risk individuals to aggressive glycaemic targets.
findings.actual_outcome: Older, comorbid participants may have been disproportionately represented in the intensive arm, contributing to observed harm.

findings.description: Hypertension control is a major determinant of cardiovascular outcomes, yet BP eligibility and management algorithms are not tightly standardised across arms.
findings.recommendation: Specify clear BP eligibility windows and harmonised BP-management algorithms across treatment strategies to avoid confounding.
findings.actual_outcome: Residual confounding by BP control complicates interpretation of treatment effects on cardiovascular endpoints.

findings.description: Creatinine- and eGFR-based dose adjustments for glucose-lowering drugs are not consistently specified or aligned across protocol sections.
findings.recommendation: Harmonise renal dosing guidance with up-to-date labelling for all agents used in the trial, and centralise these rules in a single table.
findings.actual_outcome: Inconsistent application of renal dosing rules may increase risk of adverse events and introduce heterogeneity in drug exposure.

findings.description: The achieved sample size and event rates differ from original power assumptions, but the protocol does not fully address how this affects interpretability of primary outcomes under early stopping.
findings.recommendation: Include contingency plans for lower-than-expected event rates and early stopping, with clear statistical implications.
findings.actual_outcome: Early termination and altered event accrual complicate interpretation of the primary composite outcome.
